simple_description: Sharp, burning, or shooting pain that radiates from the lower back through the buttock and down the back of the leg, caused by a pinched lumbar nerve root.
medical_description: A clinical syndrome characterized by pain radiating along the dermatomal distribution of the sciatic nerve (lumbar and sacral nerve roots L4, L5, or S1), extending past the knee into the calf and foot, typically accompanied by paresthesia, sensory deficits, motor weakness (foot drop), or diminished tendon reflexes.
affected_system: Lumbosacral nerve roots (L4, L5, S1) and the sciatic nerve trunk.
symptoms: Unilateral sharp, electric, burning, or stabbing pain shooting from lower back/buttock down the back or side of the thigh, calf, and into the foot
Pain typically worse than lower back pain itself
Aggravated by coughing, sneezing, bending forward, or prolonged sitting
Numbness, tingling, or 'pins and needles' in the dermatomal distribution (L5 top of foot, S1 sole of foot)
Motor weakness: difficulty walking on heels (L5 foot drop) or difficulty walking on toes (S1 weakness)
Depressed or absent Achilles tendon reflex (S1 radiculopathy)
early_warning_signs: Localized low back ache transitioning over days into pain traveling down into the gluteal region
possible_causes: Lumbar intervertebral disc herniation (protrusion or extrusion compressing nerve root at L4-L5 or L5-S1 - 90% of cases)
Lumbar spinal stenosis and facet joint arthropathy
Piriformis syndrome (compression of sciatic nerve by piriformis muscle)
risk_factors: Sedentary desk lifestyle with poor posture or occupations involving heavy lifting/twisting
disease_types: Cauda Equina Syndrome (SURGICAL EMERGENCY: massive central disc herniation compressing multiple lumbosacral roots)
clinical_evaluation: Straight Leg Raise (Lasègue's sign): radiating pain below the knee between 30 and 70 degrees elevation has high sensitivity; Crossed Straight Leg Raise has high specificity. Assessment of myotomes, dermatomes, and reflexes.
diagnostic_tests: High-field 3T Lumbar Spine MRI - Diagnostic gold standard: delineates disc herniation size, nerve root impingement, and spinal canal stenosis
Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS) - Confirms active denervation and chronicity after 3-4 weeks
treatment_overview: Conservative therapy resolves > 80% within 6 to 8 weeks: short relative rest (avoid prolonged bed rest), active physiotherapy, NSAIDs, neuropathic analgesia. Fluoroscopically guided epidural steroid injection for persistent severe pain. Surgical lumbar microdiscectomy indicated for progressive motor deficit (foot drop) or failure of conservative care > 6-12 weeks.
medication_classes: First-line anti-inflammatory: NSAIDs (Naproxen, Ibuprofen, Etoricoxib) for short courses
Neuropathic pain modulators: Pregabalin (75-300 mg/day) or Gabapentin (300-1800 mg/day)
Muscle relaxants (Thiocolchicoside, Baclofen) for acute spasm
precautions: AVOID prolonged strict bed rest (> 2 days); early gentle ambulation and core mobility promote faster healing
Avoid heavy deadlifting, slouching in soft couches, or sudden twisting while bent
prevention: Core muscle strengthening (McKenna / McGill Big 3 exercises)
Proper ergonomic lumbar support and correct lifting mechanics (bend knees, not waist)
complications: Permanent motor deficit (chronic foot drop requiring ankle-foot orthosis)
Chronic neuropathic lumbar radicular pain syndrome
emergency_signs: 🚨 CRITICAL SURGICAL EMERGENCY (Cauda Equina Syndrome): Call 112 / 911 or go to emergency immediately if you develop: 1. Numbness in groin, buttocks, or genitals ('saddle anesthesia'), 2. Loss of control over bladder or bowel (incontinence or inability to urinate), 3. Rapidly worsening weakness in both legs.
doctor_specialty: Spine Neurologist / Neurosurgeon / Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

faqs.question: What is Cauda Equina Syndrome and why is it an emergency?
faqs.answer: It happens when a large disc herniation crushes the cluster of nerve roots at the base of the spinal cord. It causes numbness between the legs (saddle area) and loss of bladder/bowel control. Emergency spine surgery is required within 24 to 48 hours to prevent permanent paralysis and lifelong incontinence.

hi.name: साइटिका / कमर से पैर में जाने वाला दर्द (Sciatica / Lumbar Radiculopathy)
hi.summary: कमर की नस (Sciatic nerve) दबने से कूल्हे से लेकर जांघ और पैर के पंजे तक करंट जैसा तेज दर्द, झनझनाहट या पैर में कमजोरी होना।
hi.advice: लगातार बिस्तर पर लेटे न रहें, हल्की चाल रखें और फिजियोथेरेपी करें। यदि पेशाब रुक जाए या सुन्नपन आए तो तुरंत इमरजेंसी जाएं।

hinglish.name: Sciatica (Kamar se pair me shooting pain)
hinglish.summary: Kamar me L4-L5 disc dabne se buttock se lekar poore pair ke talve tak aag jaisa dard aur sunn-pan hona.
hinglish.advice: Bed rest na karein, MRI Lumbar Spine karwayein. Saddle numbness ya urine rukne par turant emergency surgery lagti hai.

ur.name: عرق النسا (سائیٹیکا / کمر سے پاؤں کا درد)
ur.summary: کمر کے مہرے کے ہلنے سے اعصاب کا دب جانا اور کولہے سے لے کر پاؤں تک شدید درد اور سن پن۔
ur.advice: زیادہ دیر بستر پر نہ رہیں، ہلکی واک اور فزیوتھراپی کریں۔ پیشاب میں رکاوٹ کی صورت میں فوری ایمرجنسی رجوع کریں۔
